lines: - Recording captures the trusted originating chat and, when available, turn. Agent-supplied inputs cannot set provenance. Promotion and later metadata updates do not replace the origin already captured by the coordinator. Missing legacy provenance blocks automatic prompts, not manual actions.

- Observing an artifact writes nothing. A binding is stored, with the origin it was matched under, on its first change: a configuration, a manual run, or a provider checkpoint. Deleting a session, on the host or the client, removes its bindings and history once their runs settle. A run with an uncertain effect is kept, so it keeps blocking conflicting work on the resource.

-- Each consent generation records who granted it: the user, or the agent through `set_artifact_automation`. An agent grant also records whether the person confirmed that tool call or it was approved automatically, read from the call's confirmation in the chat's state; a call that cannot be identified counts as approved automatically. Manual runs record who requested them. Notices and the automation controls name agent-requested consent and say when it was auto-approved.

An agent grant also records whether the person confirmed that tool call or it was approved automatically, read from the call's confirmation in the chat's state; a call that cannot be identified counts as approved automatically. Turning a rule off records whether the user or an agent did it. Manual runs record who requested them. The automation controls name agent-requested consent and say when it was auto-approved. Notice titles name the agent, such as Copilot, Claude, or Codex, when it made every change of the notice, and notice details say when the person confirmed the agent's request.

- Settled history is bounded per binding. For each enabled option, the current generation's dispatched attempts and the latest attempt of every occurrence are kept regardless, so pruning never resets repeat protection or attempt budgets. Active, uncertain, and still-referenced runs are also kept.

- A transaction that changes nothing neither writes the ledger nor notifies observers. Repeating an occurrence that was already handled therefore returns its run without side effects, and automation contexts only report changes to their own configuration, checkpoint, or runs.

- Matching receives the artifact/reference distinction. Promotion rematches without replacing the record or its origin. A registration can invalidate matching after account changes; a different account still cannot inherit saved consent.

The shared coordinator generates consistent activity from these records. It can show queued work, native actions, prompts, failures, and skips together. Code runs get a system-authored activity entry; prompt runs link to their existing chat turn rather than duplicating it. In fallback mode, activity/history is client-local unless an existing backend API can publish it; do not fake a host transcript entry by sending a user prompt. Activity notices are not injected as model instructions.

-Runtimes with real transcript publication support expose `postNotice` for committed automation configuration transitions. Enabling a rule, changing its enabled mode, disabling it, and automatic safety disablement produce expandable system notices in the artifact's recording chat. One configuration transition of an artifact produces one notice that lists all of its rule changes. Enabled/updated notices use the artifact's primary icon and explain only what the automation does and its selected mode, not evaluation timing or attempt limits. Their expanded details open with one sentence saying that Autopilot keeps working automatically by sending messages to the agent in that chat. Disabled notices use the disabled icon and explain their reason, what happens to pending versus already-submitted work, and any other rules that remain enabled. Failed attempt counts appear only when they cause automatic disablement. Unchanged values and restored configuration do not repeat notices; failed persistence never announces a successful change.

The local host reuses its host-only local-turn publication and persistence path, independently of Agent Merge's controller. An idle chat receives the notice immediately; a busy chat receives it after its active turn finishes, without interrupting that turn or replacing a draft. Notices remain in restored history but never become provider/model requests. Routine polling and unchanged blocked states do not create transcript notices.

Bindings can also post `status` notices about a change of their resource that the person should know about, such as a pull request leaving its merge queue without merging, through the optional `postNotice` of their binding context. Their plain text is escaped, and they use the artifact's primary icon. They carry no rule changes and are never merged. Older clients render them as plain system notices.

-Consecutive notices of the same artifact merge into one. Notices carry their rule changes and each integration's enabled rules in VS Code `_meta`, and the host renders a structured notice from them rather than from client-supplied text, so a notice reads the same before and after it is merged. While the chat's last turn is the artifact's previous notice, the host replaces that turn with a notice that keeps only the latest change of each rule and the latest enabled rules of each integration. A single change keeps its specific title; several are summarized as "Autopilot enabled for {artifact} ({n} rules)" when they turn on every enabled rule of their integrations, and otherwise as "Autopilot updated for {artifact} ({n} rules)", with each rule and its explanation in the expandable details. Any other turn in between, such as an agent response, a user message, or another artifact's notice, starts a new notice, as does a merge that would exceed the limits that notice readers accept, and notices deferred during a turn merge before they are written. The replacement uses standard truncation and turn actions, so the host's state and every snapshot contain one notice. The replacement turn's message names the turn it replaces; VS Code clients remove that request when they apply the replacement, in order with other server-initiated requests. Older clients that do not read this name show both notices until the chat is reloaded. Notices from clients that send only rendered content are posted unchanged and never merged.

Prompt-backed actions also have a generic request presentation. After preparation, the executor captures the action label, integration, manual/automatic source, resource presentation, and the currently available details linked to that action or its automation option. A prepared prompt may instead supply the details it is about, such as only the failing checks a CI repair asks to fix; these replace the linked details in the snapshot and are not part of the model-facing prompt. This immutable snapshot is persisted with the run before submission and transported in the optional, validated `vscode.artifactIntegrationRequest` message metadata. Capturing details does not retain observations or fetch additional pages; incomplete or failed captures remain explicit. The snapshot never becomes an instruction or grants execution authority. While a prompt action's turn reports no activity of its own, the host describes it in the session summary by the action's optional `activityLabel`, such as "Fixing CI", or else its label, prefixed with Autopilot when an Autopilot rule ran it.
